words.prose: {{ar:ٱدْخُلِى}} ({{tr:udkhulī}}) is a direct feminine singular imperative, so the addressed soul remains the same one summoned in 89:27 and is not replaced by a crowd or impersonal recipient. Its Form I command addresses the soul's own crossing while the speaker's authority grants the access; a causative admission frame would move attention toward an outside admitting agent. The verb is not bare motion: {{ar:فِى عِبَٰدِى}} ({{tr:fī ʿibādī}}) completes it as authorized access into a servant-sphere, so the entry-request of 17:80 is answered here as granted access. The root's access and interior pressure helps the reader feel threshold-crossing into a community relation, while the local grammar keeps the sense to commanded entry rather than importing unrelated dictionary branches. The same entry command returns in 89:30 with {{ar:جَنَّتِى}} ({{tr:jannatī}}), so the close has two thresholds: first relational inclusion, then garden entry, with the compact sound of the command fitting that boundary-crossing force.

words.prose: {{ar:فِى}} ({{tr:fī}}) turns the endpoint into an inclusion sphere. The command does not make {{ar:عِبَٰدِى}} ({{tr:ʿibādī}}) a bare object; it places the soul within or among the speaker's servants, making the collective syntactically necessary rather than ornamental. That prepositional logic also marks the boundary from the prior movement toward {{ar:إِلَىٰ رَبِّكِ}} ({{tr:ilā rabbiki}}) in 89:28 to containment within a plural servant domain. In 89:30 the garden endpoint can be named more directly as {{ar:جَنَّتِى}} ({{tr:jannatī}}), so this small preposition gives 89:29 its specifically social inclusion. As a brief hinge, it also lets the line pivot audibly from command to domain before the possessed plural lands.

words.prose: {{ar:عِبَٰدِى}} ({{tr:ʿibādī}}) is the governed endpoint of {{ar:فِى}} ({{tr:fī}}), so the servants are not a second addressee but the collective into which the soul enters. The construct and final possessive make the group definite as the speaker's own, turning reward first into claimed belonging rather than generic company. The root keeps worship, service, obedience, and dependence in view; it makes the entered group a relational and conduct-shaped identity, comparable to servant conduct in 25:63, while the possessed plural also recalls the mercy summons of 39:53 now as final inclusion. The plural form makes that identity communal, many in membership but one in belonging; the singular variant {{ar:عَبْدِي}} ({{tr:ʿabdī}}) shows how much would change if the endpoint were individualized, while the local noun remains people rather than a place noun or a smooth-road image. The relation also shifts from {{ar:رَبِّكِ}} ({{tr:rabbiki}}) in 89:28 to My servants here, and then to {{ar:جَنَّتِى}} ({{tr:jannatī}}) in 89:30, so belonging comes before place, with the matching long ending of command and endpoint making the relational landing audible.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: `فَٱدْخُلِى فِى عِبَٰدِى` joins a singular imperative of entry to `فِى` and the possessed plural `عِبَٰدِى`.
baseline_models.mechanism: The command moves the addressee across a boundary into a collective whose shared principle is submissive service to the speaker. Entry therefore changes location and affiliation at once.

activation_trace.role: Going inside supplies the boundary crossing and makes the imperative an admission rather than mere proximity.
Worship and submissive obedience supply the relation that constitutes the destination collective.

changed_reading.before: A command to go inside an unspecified place near some servants.
changed_reading.after: A command to cross into belonging among those constituted by service and obedience to the speaker.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The inward branch of `د خ ل` remains attached to the imperative, while `عِبَٰدِى` names the mode entered.
baseline_models.mechanism: Entry can be inward as well as spatial: the addressee is summoned to inhabit servanthood as an interior disposition that becomes socially visible through belonging among servants.

activation_trace.role: The hidden interior turns entry toward an inward state rather than limiting it to physical relocation.
Submissive worship names the inward orientation that the addressee is invited to inhabit.

changed_reading.before: The addressee is externally relocated among a group.
changed_reading.after: The addressee enters a lived interior condition of service whose outward form is membership among the servants.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: `فِى عِبَٰدِى` can mark inclusion within a plural body, and the entry root carries images of an entrant mixing with a group and of interleaved parts.
baseline_models.mechanism: The command changes the addressee from an outsider into a constituent part of an existing servant body. Interleaving implies cohesion without requiring the entrant to disappear.

activation_trace.role: An entrant mixed into a group supplies the social transition from outsider to insider.
Interleaving parts supplies a model of close incorporation in which distinguishable parts form one body.
Shared obedient service provides the binding relation of the interleaved body.

changed_reading.before: The addressee merely stands beside a set of servants.
changed_reading.after: The addressee ceases to be an outsider and becomes an interleaved, still distinguishable member of their body.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The possessed noun `عِبَٰدِى` is capable of activating both owned status and the root's counter-image of being honored and magnified.
baseline_models.mechanism: The possessive invitation holds abasement and elevation together: entry into the speaker's servants is not simply degradation, because the same root inventory lets service coexist with being specially honored.

activation_trace.role: Literal entry makes the paradox a conferred status into which the addressee is admitted.

changed_reading.before: Entry into servanthood lowers the addressee into an owned class.
changed_reading.after: The speaker's possessive summons admits the addressee into a status where lowly service and special honor coexist.

context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies punishment, physical binding, covenant, and the owned/service branches; I infer a contrast between coercive and covenantal attachment. The alternative is simple sequencing of two outcomes with no intended comparison between fetter and servanthood.

context_deltas.mechanism: The individually addressed self remains an essence in its own right, becomes tranquil, returns to a Lord characterized by nurture and completion, and is described through paired satisfaction. Entry then becomes interleaving without erasure and service under reciprocal approval rather than anonymous absorption.

structural_cues: The vocative singles out `the tranquil self`, then the feminine imperatives `return` and `enter` preserve that addressee across the transition.

strongest_changes: The singular addressee's entry becomes a completion from lone passage into servant plurality.
The social critique revises `My servants` into a counter-community that honors the cut-off and feeds rather than consumes.
The tranquil self remains intact inside reciprocal, nurturing belonging rather than dissolving into an anonymous mass.
The repeated entry of 89:30 makes admission among the servants the first sheltering enclosure before the garden.
summary.what_was_special: The focus roots hold unusually productive tensions: entry can be inward, social, interleaving, or restorative, while servanthood can carry ownership, worship, honor, solidity, and even dispersion. Context activates these into several coexisting mechanisms rather than resolving them to one sense.
remaining_uncertainties: The early completion and even/odd sequence may resonate with singular-to-plural admission without intentionally modeling it.
The paired satisfaction forms may express mutuality, or only two parallel directions of approval.
The two entry commands may be nested stages, or coordinated welcomes without a threshold relation.
Pastoral watering, living architecture, crowd-garden overlap, and scattered-route imagery should remain analogical because their branches are distant from the ordinary surface senses.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Entry into a service-body, not isolation.** Lexical evidence: `د خ ل B001` going in/entering; `د خ ل B005` entrant mixed into a group; `ع ب د B003` worship and submissive obedience; `ع ب د B006` honoring and magnifying. Structural cue: the command follows the singular soul but moves it into `عبادي`, a collective belonging. Assigned role: entry repairs the earlier orphaned/odd isolation by joining the soul to a community of service. Abductive move: I infer that the group is defined by worshipful belonging rather than social domination, because the speaker is the Lord of return. Reading change: the ayah reads as honored incorporation, not loss of self.

2. **Hidden interior purified of defect.** Lexical evidence: `د خ ل B003` hidden interior; `د خ ل B004` hidden defect or deceit; `ن ف س B013` inner mind/intent. Structural cue: the tranquil self is commanded to enter after its inner valuation has been resolved. Assigned role: entry exposes and admits the interior that no longer carries the corrupt hidden defect. Abductive move: I infer that final inclusion requires inward truthfulness, because earlier speech concealed false doctrine. Reading change: `ادخلي` becomes an inward admission as well as spatial entry.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 89:30 sharpened this ayah’s sequence: entry into servants is the social threshold before entry into garden; belonging precedes sheltered abundance.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Entry as incorporation into a people.** **Evidence/cue:** `د خ ل B001` is going in, while `د خ ل B005` is an entrant mixed into a group or its affairs; the construction uses *fi* with the plural *ʿibadi*, not a place-name. **Mechanism:** entry's endpoint is membership, with the former singular self incorporated into a plural body. The packet supplies singular command and collective complement; I infer social integration as the result. **Reading change:** the first *udkhuli* means “become one among,” not merely cross a threshold.

2. **Servanthood as honored, willing belonging.** **Evidence/cue:** `ع ب د B003` is worship and submissive obedience, while `ع ب د B006` is honoring and magnifying; 89:28 has already established mutual approval (`ر ض و B001/B003`), and 89:26 supplied coercive restraint. **Mechanism:** service gives the group its shared orientation, but acceptance and honor distinguish that orientation from forced bondage. The packet supplies obedience, approval, and the coercive contrast; I infer willing belonging. **Reading change:** *ʿibadi* names a community dignified by shared service, not an undifferentiated owned mass.

3. **The inner self entering an inner relation.** **Evidence/cue:** `د خ ل B003` is the hidden interior of an affair, and the entrant is the *nafs*, whose `ن ف س B013` branch names inward thought and intent. **Mechanism:** the interior branch assigns entry a transformation of inward allegiance as well as social placement. The packet supplies inner self and entry; I infer that genuine incorporation reaches intention. **Reading change:** the command addresses belonging from the inside, not outward enrollment alone.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 89:30 clarified why the first complement is a people rather than a place: social incorporation precedes environmental entry. The second *udkhuli* therefore confirms `د خ ل B005` in 89:29 as group-membership, not an elliptical reference to the garden.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişinin, soyun, işin veya şeyin içinde dışarıdan hemen görünmeyen bir kusur ya da bozulma bulunur. Bu iç bozukluk kuşku, aldatma, gizli düşmanlık, zihinsel yetersizlik, çürüme veya yenme zararı biçiminde gerçekleşebilir.

Kişide zihinsel yetersizlik ya da kökende bozukluk bulunması özel bir görünüm oluşturur.

Bilmediği işlere kendini sokan kişi, araya girmenin uygunsuz ve gösterişli biçimini temsil eder.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi eklemlerin birbirine geçmesini, sinir çevresinde toplanan eti, bir renge karışan başka renkleri ve iki bölge arasında veya ağaç köklerinde kalan tüy ile otu ortak bir iç içelik ve ara konum düzeninde toplar.

concept_map.definition: Parçalar birbirinin arasına girerek birleşir, bir ana bölüm çevresinde toplanır veya iki bölüm arasında yer alır. Bu düzen eklem, et, renk, tüy ve bitki örtüsü gibi farklı maddelerde görülebilir.

facets.statement: Bir parçanın başka parçaların arasına girmesi veya onlarla iç içe birleşmesi temel ilişkidir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Toplu kanıt, parçaların iç içe geçmesi ve arada yer alması düzenini eklem, sinir çevresindeki et, renk karışımı, kuş tüyleri ve ağaç köklerindeki ot üzerinden farklı maddi görünümlerle açıklar.
